_meta.indication: Teflaro (ceftaroline fosamil) is indicated for treatment of acute bacterial skin and skin structure infections (ABSSSI) and community-acquired bacterial pneumonia (CABP) caused by susceptible isolates of the designated microorganisms.

pivotal_trials.design: Phase 3 multicenter, randomized, double-blind comparative study of ceftaroline vs. vancomycin plus aztreonam in adults with ABSSSI (noninferiority design, 10% NI margin)
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with acute bacterial skin and skin structure infections (ABSSSI)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoint: per-subject clinical cure rate at the Test-of-Cure (TOC) visit in the MITT and CE populations
pivotal_trials.result: Applicant MITT clinical cure at TOC: ceftaroline 304/351 (86.6%) vs comparator 297/347 (85.6%); difference 1.0 (95% CI -4.2, 6.2). CE: 288/316 (91.1%) vs 280/300 (93.3%); difference -2.2 (95% CI -6.6, 2.1) — noninferiority met.

pivotal_trials.design: Phase 3 multicenter, randomized, double-blind comparative study of ceftaroline vs. vancomycin plus aztreonam in adults with ABSSSI (noninferiority design, 10% NI margin)
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with acute bacterial skin and skin structure infections (ABSSSI)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoint: per-subject clinical cure rate at the Test-of-Cure (TOC) visit in the MITT and CE populations
pivotal_trials.result: Applicant MITT clinical cure at TOC: ceftaroline 291/342 (85.1%) vs comparator 289/338 (85.5%); difference -0.4 (95% CI -5.8, 5.0). CE: 271/294 (92.2%) vs 269/292 (92.1%); difference 0.1 (95% CI -4.4, 4.5) — noninferiority met.

pivotal_trials.design: Phase 3 multicenter, multinational, 1:1 randomized, double-blind, active-controlled noninferiority trial of IV ceftaroline fosamil vs IV ceftriaxone (5-7 days); two adjunctive doses of oral clarithromycin administered in P903-08
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with community-acquired bacterial pneumonia (CABP), PORT Risk Class III-IV
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Prespecified primary analysis: clinical cure rates at the test-of-cure (TOC), noninferiority margin of 10%, in MITTE and CE co-primary populations
pivotal_trials.result: Clinical cure at TOC, MITTE: ceftaroline 244/291 (83.8%) vs ceftriaxone 233/300 (77.7%); difference 6.2 (95% CI -0.2, 12.5). CE: 194/224 (86.6%) vs 183/234 (78.2%); difference 8.4 (95% CI 1.4, 15.4).

pivotal_trials.design: Phase 3 multicenter, multinational, 1:1 randomized, double-blind, active-controlled noninferiority trial of IV ceftaroline fosamil vs IV ceftriaxone (5-7 days); no adjunctive clarithromycin
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with community-acquired bacterial pneumonia (CABP), PORT Risk Class III-IV
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Prespecified primary analysis: clinical cure rates at the test-of-cure (TOC), noninferiority margin of 10%, in MITTE and CE co-primary populations
pivotal_trials.result: Clinical cure at TOC, MITTE: ceftaroline 231/284 (81.3%) vs ceftriaxone 203/269 (75.5%); difference 5.9 (95% CI -1.0, 12.8). CE: 191/232 (82.3%) vs 165/214 (77.1%); difference 5.2 (95% CI -2.2, 12.8).

key_safety: Most frequent adverse drug reactions in ceftaroline-treated patients were diarrhea (5%), nausea (4%), and rash (3%); constipation, vomiting, increased transaminases, hypokalemia, and phlebitis (2%). Direct Coombs' test seroconversion occurred more often with ceftaroline than comparator (10.8% vs 4.4%), without reported hemolytic anemia.
target_moa: Ceftaroline fosamil is an injectable prodrug of the cephalosporin class of beta-lactam antibacterials; it is bactericidal via inhibition of cell-wall synthesis by binding to penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs).

advisory_committee.vote: Anti-Infective Drugs Advisory Committee convened September 7, 2010; AIDAC unanimously agreed (18 votes to 0) both safety and efficacy were demonstrated for ABSSSI, and voted 21-0 that ceftaroline was safe and effective for CABP.

description.text: Added Clinical Studies information on acute bacterial skin and skin structure infections with concurrent S. aureus bacteraemia

citations.quote: S-013 provides for the addition of information to the Clinical Studies section (14) of the package insert regarding cases of acute bacterial skin and skin structure infections with concurrent bacteraemia caused by *Staphylococcus aureus*.

description.text: Expanded indication to include pediatric patients 2 months to less than 18 years of age for Acute Bacterial Skin and Skin Structure Infections

citations.quote: These Prior Approval Supplemental New Drug Applications provide for revisions to the **INDICATIONS AND USAGE** (1) section of the package insert to include pediatric patients 2 months to less than 18 years of age for Acute Bacterial Skin and Skin Structure Infections (S-016) and Community Acquired Bacterial Pneumonia (S-017).

description.text: Expanded ABSSSI indication to include pediatric patients from birth to less than 2 months of age

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for a change in the indicated patient population for the treatment of Acute Bacterial Skin and Skin Structure Infections (ABSSSI) to include pediatric patients from birth to less than 2 months of age.

basis.text: Fast track designation was granted February 28, 2006 by the Division of Anti-Infectives and Ophthalmology Products for the treatment of ABSSSI, based on potential to address unmet medical need including MRSA.

citations.quote: This designation was based on ceftaroline fosamil's potential to address unmet medical need for patients not responding to or unable to tolerate current treatment regimens for ABSSSI, specifically methicillin-resistant *Staphylococcus aureus* (MRSA).

summary.text: NDA 200327 for ceftaroline fosamil was submitted December 29, 2009; the program received fast track designation (granted February 28, 2006) for ABSSSI. Efficacy was supported by four Phase 3 noninferiority trials (two ABSSSI vs vancomycin/aztreonam, two CABP vs ceftriaxone). An Anti-Infective Drugs Advisory Committee convened September 7, 2010 voted unanimously in support of safety and efficacy, and the application was recommended for approval.

citations.quote: **December 29, 2009:** NDA 200327 was submitted for ceftaroline for the CABP and ABSSSI indications.

The efficacy of ceftaroline as treatment for CABP and ABSSSI is supported by clinical data from four adequate Phase 3 randomized, active-controlled, noninferiority clinical trials.

A meeting of the Anti-infective Drugs' Advisory Committee was convened on September 7, 2010, to discuss this application, and the committee members voted unanimously that the applicant had demonstrated the efficacy of ceftaroline for the treatment of CABP.

There must be a minimum of 8 evaluable subjects per cohort. In Group 3, there will be an equal representation of patients aged 28 days to <12 months and \ge 12 months to <24 months.

requirement.text: 1692-002: Randomized comparison of Teflaro vs comparator in pediatric subjects <17 years with CABP using MRSA enrichment, minimum 150 patients receiving Teflaro.

citations.quote: **1692-002:** Perform a randomized comparison of Teflaro (ceftaroline fosamil) and comparator in pediatric subjects with CABP utilizing an enrichment strategy for enrollment of patients with methicillin-resistant *Staphylococcus aureus* (MRSA). Pediatric patients under 17 years of age with CABP must be enrolled, with a minimum of 150 patients receiving Teflaro (ceftaroline fosamil).

requirement.text: 1692-003: Randomized comparison of Teflaro vs comparator in pediatric subjects <17 years with ABSSSI including suspected/demonstrated MRSA, minimum 150 patients receiving Teflaro.

Pediatric patients under 17 years of age with ABSSSI must be enrolled, with a minimum of 150 patients receiving Teflaro (ceftaroline fosamil).

citations.quote: Perform a trial assessing the CSF concentration profile of Teflaro (ceftaroline fosamil) in infants < 2 months of age. A minimum of 12 infants < 2 months of age receiving antibacterials for treatment of late-onset neonatal sepsis must be studied.

requirement.text: 1692-005: Randomized comparison of Teflaro vs comparator in infants <2 months of age with ABSSSI and CABP including suspected/demonstrated MRSA.

citations.quote: **1692-005:** Perform a randomized comparison of Teflaro (ceftaroline fosamil) and comparator in infants < 2 months of age with ABSSSI and CABP including patients with infections suspected or demonstrated to be caused by MRSA.
